candidates.name: Posterior Urethral Valves
candidates.why: The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, along with a dilated fetal bladder, suggests an obstructive uropathy, which is consistent with Posterior Urethral Valves.

candidates.name: Prune Belly Syndrome
candidates.why: The combination of bilateral renal enlargement, hydronephrosis, and a dilated bladder is also seen in Prune Belly Syndrome, which is characterized by absent or weak abdominal muscles, undescended testes, and urinary tract anomalies.

candidates.name: Ureteropelvic Junction Obstruction
candidates.why: The presence of bilateral ureteral dilation suggests an obstruction at the ureteropelvic junction, which is a common cause of hydronephrosis in infants.

candidates.name: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney
support_spans: A left perirenal fluid collection measuring 64 × 34 mm
candidates.why: The presence of a perirenal fluid collection with multiple light bands and echogenic material is suggestive of a multicystic dysplastic kidney, which is a congenital anomaly characterized by multiple cysts and dysplastic tissue.

candidates.name: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
candidates.why: The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, along with the absence of other obvious causes, raises the possibility of an inherited disorder such as Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease.
